gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a sealed over-ear pair puts about 9x the weight on your head of a bone-conduction headset (Soundcore Space One 265 g vs Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 30 g) and buys 3.3x the runtime for it (40 h ANC vs 12 h), so a 2 h/day listener charges bone conduction every 6 days but the over-ear pair every 20.
standout_why: ChatGPT's search returned no results, so there was no cited rival to check. I compared against the top organic results instead. The Shokz UK guide 'bone conduction OpenRun Pro 2 vs traditional headphones' gives the 30 g weight and 12 h playback, but its comparison table has no numbers for traditional headphones, no weight ratio and no days between charges. The HowStuffWorks, JLab, Soundcore and headphonesaddict results showed up only as search titles and snippets; their snippets compare the two types only in words (bass, awareness, isolation). Our current page lists battery hours but no weights and nothing derived.
decides: This confirms the split: bone conduction for workouts, where 30 g and no clamp on the ears matter and 12 h covers about 12 one-hour runs. Over-ear is for long listening days, where 40 h with ANC means about 20 two-hour commutes per charge, at $2.50 per rated ANC hour for the Space One against $5.00 for the Space One Pro, which has the same 40 h. That makes the Space One the value pick when ANC is the reason to choose headphones.
